title: [YouPass Collect] - Average prices of clothing imports: 1993 - 2003

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the average prices per kilometre of clothing imported into the European Union from six different countries, namely Argentina, Brazil, Japan, China, India and Bangladesh, in two separate years, 1993 and 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the average prices for clothing from Argentina, Brazil and Japan either declined or remained stable over the period, those from China, India and Bangladesh showed an upward trend. Additionally, Argentina had the highest prices throughout the period, whereas Bangladesh consistently recorded the lowest figures.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the more expensive sources, in 1993, clothing from Argentina cost £28 per kilometre, which was £5 higher than that from Brazil and almost double Japan's figure of £15. By 2003, Argentina's price had fallen slightly to £26, while Brazil's remained unchanged at £23. Similarly, Japan also experienced a modest decrease of £2, with its figure dropping to £13 at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the cheaper sources, China's clothing was priced at £10 per kilometre in 1993, followed by India at £7 and Bangladesh at only £3. Over the following decade, all three countries saw notable increases in their prices, with China rising the most significantly to £17, representing a gain of £7. Meanwhile, India's figure climbed to £12, and Bangladesh doubled its price to £6 by the end of the period, although it still remained the cheapest source of clothing imports.
